quotes.text: We ingest USMLE-style board questions and supplementary medical knowledge from flashcard decks and reference documents.

rationale: The source types are named and the paper describes provenance from task instances back to source material. The packet does not give source versions or snapshot dates/platforms for the medical-education materials, so this is partial.

quotes.text: Synthetic Hospital is built entirely from publicly available medical-education material containing no protected health information.

rationale: The paper states origin and broad provenance, and the README separately states released data are redistributable. It does not document the source materials' licences or terms plus consent/IRB status, so this is partial.

quotes.text: Synthetic Hospital closely matches the ICD-10 chapter distribution of its source corpus

rationale: The appendix compares case mix against its source corpus and a named population-oriented Synthea cohort. It reports divergence from the population-calibrated comparator and explicitly characterizes representativeness limits.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code excerpts, and S5 prompts/tool descriptions. The packet reports realism, graph-label validation, leakage controls, and limitations, but no dedicated unsafe-output or bias tests.

quotes.text: no chart or source material crosses split boundaries

rationale: The benchmark uses patient-level held-out splits and reports split-boundary controls. It also reports diagnosis overlap/unseen-diagnosis measurements across splits, satisfying a control plus measured check.

quotes.text: postgres and redis are on an internal network the agent container is not attached to

rationale: The Harbor and environment docs state the agent token cannot read labels or rewards and name network/credential mechanisms. The README also discloses an older leaky eval/agents harness, but the documented environment/Harbor mechanism satisfies this item.

The release pins a v1.3 tag and includes the benchmark database, simulator, scorer, RL environment, and packaging. The scorer is deterministic at evaluation time; external live calls are for the model under test.
The Harbor task export includes an oracle solution and states its expected perfect score. The README also gives a self-check command for running the oracle.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code excerpts, and S5 prompts/tool descriptions. The benchmark tasks are answer-submission tasks over a read-only EHR record; no task requires changing clinical environment state, so the NA clause applies.

quotes.text: a malformed or empty submission scores 0 rather than raising

rationale: The docs state trivial malformed/empty submissions receive zero and describe task metrics requiring structured clinical content. No empirical random-agent or chance-rate result is reported for all tasks.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code excerpts, and S5 prompts/tool descriptions. The packet includes model, physician, oracle, and scripted demo material, but no do-nothing or random agent score report for the benchmark tasks.

quotes.text: The graph recovered 111 of the 119 relationships (93%)

rationale: The benchmark validates ontology-derived labels against independent physician judgment and reports agreement figures. This is validation of its own label construction/evaluator basis on benchmark outputs.

The docs report deterministic sampling for the RL environment and the paper describes deterministic pipeline stages. The packet does not state a repeated-run policy for the harness, so this is partial.
The paper reports ranges and some tests/CIs for validation and robustness analyses. It does not provide a CI or significance test for the headline model-to-model leaderboard comparison.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code excerpts, and S5 prompts/tool descriptions. The packet reports numbers of instances and models, but not number of independent runs per headline score, seed/decoding policy for those runs, or independence of runs.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code excerpts, and S5 prompts/tool descriptions. Model headline scores are reported as point estimates without CI/SE, resampling unit, or clustering treatment.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code excerpts, and S5 prompts/tool descriptions. The packet does not report identical reruns, action-sequence agreement, final-state agreement, or pass^k metrics.

The harness/release is pinned by tag, but the reported model names are family-style names rather than provider snapshot IDs or dated model identifiers. S1-S3 do not report full decoding parameters for the reported evaluations.

The docs specify OpenAI-style function schemas and describe some error/failure behavior, including bad arguments and malformed submissions. They do not document read/write side effects per tool across every tool, and that property does not clearly reach the agent-visible surface.

quotes.text: The completed records are served through a production-style clinical environment

rationale: The benchmark discloses that the EHR is a simulated clinical environment. S1-S3 do not report tool conformance test results, and the simulation disclosure is not shown to reach the agent-visible prompt/tool surface.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code excerpts, and S5 prompts/tool descriptions. The packet's benchmark actions are chart-reading/searching and answer submission; no agent action represents a clinical order, prescription, note, message, or other clinical-state write, so the NA clause applies.

quotes.text: Rewards are the tasks' primary metrics

rationale: The docs state that submissions are graded by task primary metrics over submitted answer strings, not end-state changes. They justify non-state grading through graph-derived labels, but do not report validation on injected correct and incorrect outcomes with per-class error rates.

quotes.text: Assessment and plan sections are stripped from every observation

rationale: The docs describe tool-channel leakage controls and a held-out split, though README says heldout reference labels are shipped for local scoring. No canary or task-level provenance marker for released tasks is reported.

quotes.text: For each task, we report the standardized input, expected output, primary evaluation metric

rationale: Results are reported per task family, and task instance counts are reported. Although demographic fields exist, the packet does not report model results sliced by patient demographic subgroups.

quotes.text: The released data files are fully synthetic and redistributable

rationale: The packet states the environment records are synthetic and gives redistribution terms separate from code licence. It does not report an IRB determination, DUA/credentialing requirement, or de-identification method for real data governance.
